papers.title: Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney.
papers.abstract: Sequence-to-function (S2F) deep learning models predict genome-wide functional profiles directly from DNA sequences and have significantly advanced our understanding of gene regulation. However, existing S2F models are fundamentally constrained by their initial training datasets, and no single model encompasses the full spectrum of cell types, clinical conditions, and cellular states, while training new models de novo is nontrivial. Here, we develop Kidzoi, a kidney cell-type-specific S2F model obtained by transfer learning from the pretrained model Borzoi using single-nucleus chromatin access
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Kidzoi is a kidney cell-type-specific sequence-to-function deep learning model created by transfer learning from the pretrained Borzoi model using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data. It enables prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects in specific kidney cell types, addressing the limitation that no single pretrained model covers all cell types and clinical conditions. This approach provides a practical way to adapt existing models to new tissues without training de novo.

papers.title: Integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics for deciphering prognostic value and immunotherapeutic features of floatptosis-mediated cell death in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Recent research has uncovered an unprecedented cell death pathway induced by outer membrane vesicles derived from Bergeyella cardium variant (BCV). This process promotes the pathological fusion of lysosome-related organelles via the SLC9A9 protein, leading to the formation of large vacuoles and ultimately inducing a terminal vacuolar cell death termed floatptosis. However, the role of floatptosis-related genes (FRGs) in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains largely unexplored. In this study, we constructed a LUAD prognostic model based on FRGs to predict patient prognosis and further explored the
papers.summary: The authors built a prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes related to floatptosis, a newly described vacuolar cell death pathway triggered by outer membrane vesicles from a Bergeyella cardium variant. Using integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, they link these genes to patient survival and immunotherapeutic features. The work is exploratory and the clinical utility of the model remains to be validated.

papers.title: Multi-omics and pathological landscape of a senescence-associated prognostic model in bladder urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence contributes to tumor progression and shapes the tumor microenvironment (TME), yet its prognostic and biological significance in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA) remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify senescence-associated prognostic signals through pan-cancer screening and to develop an integrated risk stratification framework for BLCA that bridges molecular characterization with translational relevance.
papers.summary: This study identifies cellular senescence-associated gene signatures through pan-cancer screening and builds a prognostic risk model for bladder urothelial carcinoma. The model integrates multi-omics and pathological data to stratify patients and characterize the tumor microenvironment, linking senescence biology to clinical outcomes.

papers.title: PoolParty: streamlined design of DNA sequence libraries in Python.
papers.abstract: Computationally designed DNA sequence libraries are essential components of massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs), deep mutational scanning (DMS) experiments, and other multiplex assays of variant effect (MAVEs). They are also increasingly used in silico to analyze genomic AI models. Designing these libraries, however, remains tedious and error-prone due to the scarcity of purpose-built software.
papers.summary: PoolParty is a Python package that streamlines the design of computationally generated DNA sequence libraries used in massively parallel reporter assays, deep mutational scanning, and other multiplex assays of variant effect. It addresses the lack of purpose-built software, which makes library design tedious and error-prone, and also supports in silico analysis of genomic AI models.

papers.title: Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data.
papers.abstract: The explosion of microbial omics data has outpaced the ability of many researchers to analyse it, with complex tools and limited computational resources creating barriers to discovery. To address this gap, we present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL): a free, globally accessible, community-supported platform that combines state-of-the-art analytical power with user-friendly accessibility. Supported by the Galaxy and global microbiology communities, this platform integrates over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows, enabling comprehensive metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, (meta)transcriptomic,
papers.summary: The authors present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL), a free, community-supported web platform that gives microbiologists access to over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows for reproducible, FAIR analysis of metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, and (meta)transcriptomic data. The platform aims to lower computational and technical barriers that currently prevent many researchers from analyzing the rapidly growing volume of microbial omics data.

papers.title: Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous non-coding risk variants for prostate and ovarian cancers, yet determining which are regulatorily active and which target genes they control remains challenging. We re-analysed a dinucleotide-barcode massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) of 208 bi-allelic prostate cancer risk single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in three prostate cancer cell lines under false-discovery-rate (FDR) control, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10 (30 at FDR < 0.05), including 9 shared by at least two cell lines. Benchmarking standard in
papers.summary: The authors re-analyzed a massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) testing 208 prostate cancer risk SNPs in three cell lines, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10. They then benchmarked standard in silico annotation tools against these experimental results and used the findings to prioritize ovarian cancer risk variants by cross-cancer comparison. This provides a resource for evaluating computational predictions of regulatory variants and a framework for hypothesis generation across cancer types.

papers.title: Agent_K: An Agent-Orchestrated Pipeline for Mapping Genes to Biosynthetic Pathway towards Metabolite Discovery.
papers.abstract: The identification of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) and their associated metabolic pathways is central to genome-guided natural product discovery. However, existing computational tools depend on fragmented workflows for data processing, annotation, and analysis, which require substantial manual intervention and lack seamless integration across heterogeneous platforms and tools. Here, we present, Agent_K, an agent-orchestrated framework that automates the end-to-end process from bacterial whole genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic pathway mapping and metabolite discovery as candidate ge
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Agent_K is an agent-orchestrated framework that automates the entire workflow from bacterial whole-genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) identification, pathway mapping, and candidate metabolite discovery. It addresses the fragmentation of existing computational tools by integrating data processing, annotation, and analysis across heterogeneous platforms with minimal manual intervention. This enables more efficient genome-guided natural product discovery.

papers.title: Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk.
papers.abstract: Disease-relevant changes in RNA processing frequently evade detection because they are missing from transcript annotations. Here, we introduce Torino , a computational framework that learns patterns of RNA processing directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data by modeling how coverage varies across samples, in datasets spanning tissues, individuals and disease states. Torino adapts non-negative matrix factorization to decompose coverage into patterns that capture RNA processing events, and to quantify their usage across samples, without transcript annotations. Across seven vertebrate sp
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present Torino, a computational framework that discovers RNA processing patterns directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data without relying on existing transcript annotations. By adapting non-negative matrix factorization to model coverage variation across samples, Torino identifies unannotated RNA processing events and links them to disease risk across tissues, individuals, and disease states in seven vertebrate species.

papers.title: Streamline CNV - A Handy Nextflow Pipeline for Chromosomal Copy Number Variation Analysis.
papers.abstract: Aneuploidy, characterized by imbalanced chromosomal copy number variation (CNV), occurs in both normal somatic tissues and a wide range of diseases. Low pass whole genome sequencing (LP-WGS) to detect CNVs in cells and tissues has been widely used in all biological research. Existing informatics tools for detecting CNV often require computational expertise, often posing challenges for wet-lab biologists. To address this need, we developed Streamline CNV (SLCNV) - a user-friendly and flexible copy number analysis pipeline that allows researchers to perform many copy number-related analyses step
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SLCNV is a user-friendly Nextflow pipeline that automates chromosomal copy number variation analysis from low-pass whole genome sequencing data, addressing the barrier that existing CNV detection tools pose for wet-lab biologists. It provides a flexible, streamlined workflow covering multiple copy number-related analysis steps without requiring computational expertise.

papers.title: Combining MAVEs and computational predictors improves variant classification across ancestries in hereditary cancer genes.
papers.abstract: Many commonly used computational tools for variant effect prediction exhibit ancestry-related bias because they are trained on clinical or population datasets that under-represent global diversity, leading to uneven and sometimes unfair variant classification across ancestries. Multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs) and population-free variant effect predictors (VEPs) instead offer alternatives that are unbiased with respect to human ancestry, providing classification evidence that generalises across populations.
papers.summary: This paper shows that commonly used computational variant effect predictors are biased by ancestry because their training data under-represent global populations, leading to unequal classification of variants in hereditary cancer genes. The authors demonstrate that combining multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs) with population-free predictors provides ancestry-unbiased evidence that generalizes across populations, improving fair variant classification.

papers.title: Single-cell variant landscape of the human mitochondrial genome reveals cell type-specific functions and disease mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) heteroplasmy is a significant source of cellular genetic diversity and can cause disease yet its distribution and functional importance across different human cell types are poorly understood. Here we present scMOCHA (Single-Cell Mitochondrial Omics for Cellular Heteroplasmy Analysis), a scalable computational framework that resolves high-confidence, single-cell resolution mtDNA heteroplasmy directly from standard single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. Using this tool to interrogate publicly available scRNA-seq datasets from human peripheral blood mononuclear ce
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present scMOCHA, a scalable computational framework that infers high-confidence single-cell mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy directly from standard scRNA-seq data. Applying it to public human PBMC datasets, they uncover cell type-specific patterns of mtDNA variants and link them to cellular functions and disease mechanisms. This enables mitochondrial genetic diversity to be studied at single-cell resolution without specialized assays.

papers.title: Catalytic DNA for Precision Diagnostics: DNAzyme-Based Approaches to Single-Nucleotide Polymorphism Detection.
papers.abstract: Single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) are the most abundant form of human genetic variation and serve as important biomarkers in disease risk assessment, therapeutic stratification, and precision medicine. Yet accurate detection of low-abundance SNPs in complex biological samples remains difficult with many conventional genotyping methods, which often rely on sophisticated instrumentation and show limited tolerance to matrix interference. DNAzyme-based biosensors offer a promising alternative by coupling programmable nucleic acid recognition with catalytic signal generation under isothermal c
papers.journal: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology
papers.summary: This review discusses DNAzyme-based biosensors as a strategy for detecting single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), the most common form of human genetic variation and key biomarkers for disease risk and precision medicine. It argues that these catalytic nucleic acid sensors can achieve accurate SNP detection in complex biological samples without sophisticated instrumentation, overcoming limitations of conventional genotyping methods such as matrix interference and low-abundance target detection.

papers.title: Ultrafast alignment-free detection of viral genome variation with bronko.
papers.abstract: As viral sequencing datasets continue to grow, traditional alignment-based variant calling pipelines are becoming computationally prohibitive. To address these challenges, we developed bronko, an ultrafast alignment-free framework for detecting viral variation directly from sequencing data. The novel computational approach implemented in bronko allows scaling to massive viral sequencing datasets and has four key components: i) a locality-sensitive bucketing function to rapidly identify single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) relative to reference(s), ii) a direct k-mer count pseudo-mapping appr
papers.summary: The authors present bronko, an alignment-free framework that detects viral genome variation directly from sequencing reads using locality-sensitive bucketing and k-mer counting, avoiding the computational cost of traditional alignment-based variant calling. This approach enables scaling to massive viral sequencing datasets while rapidly identifying SNPs relative to reference genomes.

papers.title: Leveraging artificial intelligence for livestock genetics and breeding.
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming modern society including animal genetics and breeding which is essential for meeting global nutritional needs in supplying milk, meat, and eggs among the most complete sources of protein and micronutrients. Although animal breeding has a long history of using data-driven prediction methods, the application of modern AI approaches remains at a relatively early stage and shows substantial potential for wide-ranging applications in animal genetics and breeding. This study aims to review the current use of AI tools in livestock
papers.journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence tools are currently applied in livestock genetics and breeding, noting that while animal breeding has long relied on data-driven prediction, modern AI methods are still at an early stage of adoption. The authors highlight the broad potential for AI to improve selection, prediction, and breeding decisions in cattle, poultry, and other livestock, and identify opportunities for wider application.

papers.title: Integrated optimization of experimental and computational workflows improves genome recovery in long-read gut metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Short-read metagenomic sequencing has been widely applied in microbial research due to its high quality and decreasing cost. However, short reads are inherently fragmented, which limits assembly contiguity and the recovery of complete microbial genomes. In contrast, long-read sequencing, with significantly longer read lengths, helps overcome these limitations. Achieving complete and accurate genome recovery is the core goal of metagenomics. To address this challenge, we systematically evaluated and optimized the long-read metagenomic workflow, from sample processing to computational assembly,
papers.summary: This study systematically optimizes a long-read metagenomics workflow for gut microbiome samples, spanning sample processing through computational assembly, to improve recovery of complete microbial genomes. By integrating experimental and computational tuning, the authors show that end-to-end workflow optimization yields better assembly contiguity and genome recovery than default approaches. The work provides practical guidance for researchers seeking high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes from long-read data.

papers.title: Proteomics-Guided Discovery of Candidate Enzymes for Degradation of a Rare Pyruvylated Glycosaminogalactan by a Newly Isolated Luteolibacter Strain.
papers.abstract: Bacterial exopolysaccharides (EPS) display extensive structural diversity arising from variation in monosaccharide composition, glycosidic linkages, and non-carbohydrate modifications. However, the enzymes responsible for degrading many EPS structures remain unknown, reflecting the limited coverage of current carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) families. Here, we investigated the microbial degradation of EPSLp, a high-molecular-mass glycosaminogalactan from Lactiplantibacillus pentosus KW1 containing the uncommon GalNAcβ1 → 2(4,6-O-R-pyruvyl)Gal motif. Enrichment cultivation with EPSLp as the
papers.summary: The authors isolated a new Luteolibacter strain capable of degrading a rare pyruvylated glycosaminogalactan exopolysaccharide (EPSLp) from Lactiplantibacillus pentosus. Using proteomics to identify enzymes induced during growth on EPSLp, they discovered candidate carbohydrate-active enzymes responsible for degrading this uncommon structure. This work expands knowledge of CAZyme diversity and bacterial polysaccharide degradation pathways.

papers.title: Conservative evolution of genetic and features in Caenorhabditis becei, an experimentally tractable gonochoristic worm.
papers.abstract: Caenorhabditis nematodes represent a promising model clade for evolutionary genetics and genomics, but research has focused on the three androdioecious species, those with self-fertile hermaphrodites, all in the Elegans Group of species. The majority of Caenorhabditis species are gonochorists, with males and females, characterized by inconveniently high heterozygosity and inbreeding depression. We have identified C. becei as an experimentally tractable gonochorist. We show that transmission-genetic properties known from the androdioecious Elegans Group species are conserved in this Japonica Gr
papers.summary: The authors identify Caenorhabditis becei, a gonochoristic (male-female) nematode, as an experimentally tractable model for evolutionary genetics. They show that transmission-genetic properties previously characterized in the self-fertile Elegans Group species are conserved in this Japonica Group species, despite its obligate outcrossing lifestyle. This expands the toolkit of Caenorhabditis models beyond the hermaphroditic Elegans Group.

papers.title: Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges.
papers.abstract: Plant breeding is entering a multimodal era in which genomic, phenotypic, environmental, and multi-omics data are generated alongside a rapidly expanding scientific literature. Text-based large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, and biological foundation models (Bio-FMs) offer complementary capabilities for organizing evidence, representing biological relationships, and learning from molecular data. Here, we review these technologies across knowledge mining, predictive modeling, and intelligent breeding design, and apply a systematic evidence audit to dis
papers.summary: This review examines how large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, and biological foundation models can support predictive plant breeding by integrating genomic, phenotypic, environmental, and multi-omics data with scientific literature. The authors survey applications across knowledge mining, predictive modeling, and intelligent breeding design, and perform a systematic evidence audit to assess the strength of claims in this emerging field.

papers.title: A recall-rescue fuzzy layer over paired Z-DNA Hunter scans for fast Z-DNA detection.
papers.abstract: Accurate detection of Z-DNA-forming regions is limited by the trade-off between sensitivity and specificity in sequence-based methods. We present Z-DNA-Fuzzy Hunter 1.1.0-a fast and interpretable protocol that extends Z-DNA Hunter through a dual-scan strategy combined with a fuzzy expert layer. A permissive scan (model 2, minimum length 6 bp, threshold 30%) captures a broad candidate set, while a stringent scan (model 2, minimum length 10 bp, threshold 60%) provides high-confidence support. These outputs are integrated using fuzzy inference incorporating sequence signal, cross-scan support, ge
papers.summary: The authors present Z-DNA-Fuzzy Hunter 1.1.0, a tool that improves detection of Z-DNA-forming regions by combining a permissive scan (broad candidate capture) with a stringent scan (high-confidence support) and integrating the results through a fuzzy expert layer. This dual-scan plus fuzzy inference strategy aims to overcome the sensitivity-specificity trade-off in sequence-based Z-DNA prediction while remaining fast and interpretable.

papers.title: Inferring causal networks for genomic trios with high-dimensional confounding variables.
papers.abstract: Causal structure inference under the principle of Mendelian randomization (PMR) enables the study of causal relationships between two molecular phenotypes (e.g. gene expression) by leveraging genetic variants as instrumental variables to impose constraints on edge direction. In practice, inference is often affected by numerous confounding variables, such as other genes, other processes and demographic variables, making it essential to robustly account for confounders. However, existing methods have limited ability to accommodate high-dimensional confounding. Here, we introduce Mendelian random
papers.summary: The paper introduces a new method for inferring causal relationships between molecular phenotypes (like gene expression) using genetic variants as instruments under Mendelian randomization, while accounting for high-dimensional confounding variables such as other genes, processes, and demographics. Existing methods struggle with many confounders, so this work aims to robustly handle them in causal network inference for genomic trio data.

papers.title: SCCmecExtractor: a tool for extracting staphylococcal cassette chromosome elements from whole-genome sequences.
papers.abstract: Staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements are mobile genetic elements that integrate at the rlmH gene and are predominantly responsible for methicillin resistance in staphylococci. Although staphylococcal cassette chromosome mec (SCCmec) typing tools exist, none can extract the element sequence itself or explicitly classify SCC elements that lack methicillin resistance genes. Here, we present SCCmecExtractor, a lightweight Python toolkit that identifies SCC element boundaries through degenerate attachment site (att) pattern matching, extracts complete elements from whole-genome assembl
papers.summary: SCCmecExtractor is a new lightweight Python tool that identifies and extracts complete staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements from whole-genome assemblies by detecting degenerate attachment site patterns. Unlike existing SCCmec typing tools, it can extract the full element sequence and classify SCC elements even when they lack methicillin resistance genes. This enables more comprehensive analysis of these mobile genetic elements in staphylococci.

papers.title: The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria.
papers.abstract: Metabolic traits mediate microbial interactions and underpin mechanistic models of community assembly. With the rapid expansion of genomic data and bioinformatic tools, it is widely assumed that metabolic traits such as substrate utilization can be reliably inferred from genomes alone. Here, we systematically evaluate this assumption by comparing genome-based predictions from four commonly used tools to high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria. For simple substrates, prediction accuracy was limited and highly variable across taxa and substrates, with many strains predicted at o
papers.summary: This study systematically tested whether metabolic traits like substrate utilization can be reliably predicted from bacterial genomes alone. Comparing four common bioinformatic tools against high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria, the authors found that prediction accuracy was limited and highly variable across taxa and substrates, especially for simple substrates. The results caution against assuming that genome-based metabolic predictions are universally reliable.

papers.title: Long-read sequencing of FLG identifies extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and detects rare loss-of-function variants.
papers.abstract: Loss-of-function (LOF) variants of the FLG gene are risk factors for atopic dermatitis. However, owing to the repetitive nature of exon 3, these variants are difficult to characterize. We sought to determine whether the use of long-read technologies would enable better characterization of the FLG gene and improve the detection of LOF variants. We sequenced a diverse clinical cohort of 192 samples collected in Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda using long-read sequencing as well as publicly available data. We identified both common and rare LOF variants linked to atopic dermatitis in our clinical coh
papers.journal: JID innovations : skin science from molecules to population health
papers.summary: This study used long-read sequencing to characterize the repetitive exon 3 of the FLG gene in a diverse cohort of 192 samples from Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda. They found extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and identified both common and rare loss-of-function variants associated with atopic dermatitis, demonstrating that long-read technology improves variant detection in this difficult-to-sequence region.

papers.title: Ultra-deep HiFi sequencing reveals rare structural-variant subpopulations in multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa from an LVAD-associated infection.
papers.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a Gram-negative opportunistic pathogen frequently associated with multidrug-resistant infections in clinical settings. The rise of antibiotic-resistant strains and their genomic complexity necessitate advanced tools for comprehensive genetic characterization, particularly in the context of resistance to antibiotic and phage therapies.
papers.summary: The authors used ultra-deep HiFi long-read sequencing to characterize a multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate from a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) infection, uncovering rare structural-variant subpopulations within the bacterial population. This demonstrates that standard sequencing depth can miss clinically relevant genomic heterogeneity in resistant pathogens, which matters for both antibiotic and phage therapy development.

papers.title: Genomic profiling and drug resistance patterns of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Indonesia: whole-genome sequencing of isolates from the 2017-2018 national Tuberculosis Drug Resistance Survey.
papers.abstract: Drug-resistant tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia. This study aimed to characterize the genetic diversity, lineage distribution, and genotypic resistance profiles of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates across the Indonesian archipelago using whole-genome sequencing.
papers.summary: This study used whole-genome sequencing to characterize Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Indonesia's 2017–2018 national drug resistance survey, mapping lineage distribution and genotypic resistance profiles across the archipelago. It provides a nationwide genomic baseline for drug-resistant TB in Indonesia, a high-burden setting where such data were previously limited.

papers.title: Design and validation of nucleosome binding peptides using BindCraft.
papers.abstract: Chromatin is a sophisticated assembly of DNA, RNA and proteins in the nuclei of eukaryotic cells. Protein-protein interactions that govern chromatin function are key regulators of genome activity, making them prime targets for drug discovery. Engineering and modulating these contacts presents a viable pathway for innovative epigenetic therapies. Nucleosomes, the primary structural units of chromatin, feature various interaction interfaces, most notably the acidic patch. This region serves as a critical binding site for numerous chromatin-associated proteins, often via their intrinsically disor
papers.summary: This paper describes the design and validation of peptide binders targeting the nucleosome acidic patch using BindCraft, a computational protein design tool. The authors demonstrate that de novo designed peptides can bind nucleosomes at this key chromatin interface, suggesting a route toward engineered epigenetic modulators. The work provides proof-of-concept for computational design of chromatin-binding peptides as potential drug-discovery leads.

papers.title: Assembly and comparative analysis of the mitochondrial genome of Pteroceltis tatarinowii Maxim. (Cannabaceae), a tertiary relict plant endemic to China.
papers.abstract: Pteroceltis tatarinowii Maxim. (Cannabaceae) is a deciduous arbor endemic to China. As a Tertiary relict plant, it is listed as a rare and endangered species under national Class III key protection. Mitochondrial genomic data of P. tatarinowii can improve our knowledge of phylogenetic relationships within Cannabaceae, resolve the taxonomic placement and evolutionary divergence of the genus Pteroceltis, and supply molecular support for conservation and genetic breeding of this endangered tree.
papers.summary: This study assembled and analyzed the mitochondrial genome of Pteroceltis tatarinowii, a rare Tertiary relict tree endemic to China. The mitochondrial genomic data were used to clarify phylogenetic relationships within Cannabaceae and the evolutionary placement of the genus Pteroceltis, providing molecular resources for conservation and breeding of this endangered species.

papers.title: ogMapper improves speed and memory for short-sequencing read mapping using a novel guided sparse genome index.
papers.abstract: Short DNA-read sequencing has become an everyday essential tool in research and clinical setting. Read mapping is a crucial step that consumes large amounts of memory and CPU time, limiting the hardware required and ultimately restricting its applications. The memory required for the genome index can be approximated as βG, where G is the genome size and β is a factor that depends on the implementation. For example, β ≈ 10 for bwa-mem2 or β ≈ 1.9 for minimap2. Here, an indexing strategy is presented in which β can be even less than 1, commonly around 0.5. The indexing strategy relies on "guides
papers.summary: ogMapper introduces a new genome indexing strategy for short-read mapping that reduces the memory footprint of the genome index to roughly half the genome size (β ≈ 0.5), compared with β ≈ 1.9 for minimap2 and β ≈ 10 for bwa-mem2. The approach uses a 'guided sparse' index, aiming to lower both memory and CPU requirements so that read mapping can run on more modest hardware.

papers.title: pycircdb: integrated circRNA database annotation for computational workflows.
papers.abstract: Currently, multiple databases exist for the annotation of circular RNAs, providing descriptions of their genomic features, FASTA sequences, predicted microRNA targets and RNA-binding protein interactions. Despite the availability of these resources, annotation remains cumbersome. Conflicting identifiers and genomic coordinates for circular RNAs across databases pose a challenge to reproducibility for users. Furthermore, current databases primarily provide access via web-based graphical user interfaces, bulk downloads and limited programmatic access, rendering their use in computational workflo
papers.summary: pycircdb is a new Python package that integrates multiple circRNA databases into a unified annotation resource, resolving conflicting identifiers and genomic coordinates across sources. It provides programmatic access designed for computational workflows, addressing the limitations of web-based interfaces and bulk downloads. This enables reproducible circRNA annotation in bioinformatics pipelines.

papers.title: vardictcpp: a C++ reimplementation of VarDict variant caller.
papers.abstract: Genomic variant calling is a central computational task in disease research and diagnostics, where somatic mutations such as JAK2 V617F serve as diagnostic markers in myeloid neoplasms. VarDict, originally written in Perl, and its reimplementation VarDictJava are widely used variant callers in the bioinformatics community. The Perl implementation requires run times of up to several hours; VarDictJava reduces this to a few minutes but can consume large amounts of main memory, which limits the number of jobs that can be run in parallel on a given machine. We present vardictcpp, a functionally id
papers.summary: vardictcpp is a C++ reimplementation of the widely used VarDict variant caller, aiming to improve on the slow Perl original and the memory-hungry VarDictJava. It preserves the same functionality while offering faster runtimes and lower memory use, enabling more parallel jobs on a single machine.
